title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

reading.body:
This is a data handling failure in a developer tool, not a model error. A feature that was on by default sent local code repositories to a cloud service without the users' consent. The failure sits in the deployment defaults of the coding assistant, in the path that moves local files off the machine, rather than in anything the assistant generated or recommended.

Catching it would have required treating the upload path as a consent boundary rather than a convenience. A default-off setting, a clear prompt before any repository left the machine, or egress monitoring on the client would each have surfaced the transfer before developers found it themselves. The later patch and the disabling of the upload path address the mechanism, but the exposure window is what the reporting describes.

What is not established is intent, and the retracted claim about six workspaces containing sensitive data is not a finding. The independent reviews reporting no retained code data are Z.ai's account, not an external determination.

reports.title: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue

summary: Z.ai disabled features of its ZCode AI coding assistant after developers reported that local code repositories were uploaded to Alibaba Cloud without consent. Z.ai said a default-enabled Codebase Indexing feature caused the behavior, apologized, patched the vulnerability, and later disabled the upload path. One company retracted a separate claim that six workspaces containing sensitive data had been uploaded. Z.ai said independent reviews found no code data retained.
title_en: China's Z.ai disables AI coding assistant features after security issue
